Battle of Passchendaele.fact: No ground captured by the British was lost and German counter-attacks managed only to reach ground to which survivors of the front-line divisions had retired. German artillery began a bombardment between the Menin road and the Reutelbeek.

Battle of Passchendaele.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Battle of Passchendaele.fact: The German 4th Army was prevented from transferring troops away from the Fifth Army and from concentrating its artillery-fire on the Canadians as they prepared for the Second Battle of Passchendaele (26 October – 10 November 1917). The Germans lost 38,000 men killed or missing and 12,000 prisoners, along with 200 guns and 720 machine-guns, against 14,000 French casualties, fewer than a third of the German total.

Battle of Passchendaele.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Battle of Passchendaele.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Passchendaele.question: Expanding the salient would make the troops in it less vulnerable to _____ artillery-fire and provide a better jumping off line for a resumption of the offensive in the spring of 1918
Battle of Passchendaele.fact: The area was subjected to constant German artillery bombardments and its vulnerability to attack led to a suggestion by Brigadier C. F. Aspinall, that either the British should retire to the west side of the Gheluvelt Plateau or advance to broaden the salient towards Westroosebeke. Expanding the salient would make the troops in it less vulnerable to German artillery-fire and provide a better jumping off line for a resumption of the offensive in the spring of 1918.

Battle of Passchendaele.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Passchendaele.question: In the moonlight, the _____ could see the British troops when they were still 200 yd (180 m) away
Battle of Passchendaele.fact: The British attacked towards Westroozebeke on the night of 1/2 December but the plan to mislead the Germans, by not bombarding the German defences until eight minutes after the infantry advanced, came undone. The noise of the British assembly and the difficulty of moving across muddy and waterlogged ground had also alerted the Germans.

Battle of Passchendaele.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Battle of Passchendaele.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The _____ was 657 battle of the First Fitna.
Battle of Siffin.fact: The Battle of Siffin (Arabic: معركة صفّين, romanized: Maʿraka Ṣiffīn) was fought in 657 CE (37 AH) between the Iraqi Arab forces of the fourth Rashidun caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib and the Syrian Arab forces of the rebelling long-time governor of the Levant, Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy

Battle of Siffin.fact: The battle is named after its location Siffin on the banks of the Euphrates river.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The fighting stopped after the _____ called for arbitration when Ali's forces started to gain the upper hand, to which Ali reluctantly agreed under pressure from some of his troops
Battle of Siffin.fact: The fighting stopped after the Syrians called for arbitration when Ali's forces started to gain the upper hand, to which Ali reluctantly agreed under pressure from some of his troops. The arbitration process ended inconclusively in 658 though it strengthened the Syrians' support for Mu'awiya and his political position while weakening the authority of Ali and causing dissension among the Iraqis.

Battle of Siffin.subject: Indian Archaeology & Epigraphy
Battle of Siffin.question: The battle was part of the _____ and is considered a major step towards the establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate
Battle of Siffin.fact: The battle was part of the First Fitna and is considered a major step towards the establishment of the Umayyad Caliphate.
